assessment: There is no sideboard, so all ten are pool scouts. The audit names two real holes and the ten answers both: interaction-breadth covers one of five permanent classes, and the Mikaeus half of the deck's second declared kill is a single card at 9.5% assembly. Beast Within plus Scavenging Ooze moves breadth from one class to five — the cited target, exactly — and Gravecrawler, Reassembling Skeleton and Forsaken Miner give that kill three routes that never name Mikaeus, each with every partner already sleeved. Ramp sits four copies over the 10-12 target, which is what funds the ten: four of the cuts come from there. Three famous names stay off. The Great Henge (rank 235) prices off greatest power, and a board of 1/1 Snakes leaves it near nine mana. Triskelion wants Mikaeus for a line in-deck Walking Ballista already runs. Peer into the Abyss is seven mana in a deck whose modal cost is two, and it carries no role and no synergy shortlist at all.

ten.why: One mana that comes back every turn from the graveyard as long as a Zombie is out, and the deck already controls three — Carrion Feeder, Host of the Hereafter and Mikaeus — so it is permanent Yawgmoth fodder from turn 2 and the three-card lines with Pitiless Plunderer need nothing the deck does not already own.

ten.why: Recomputing the breadth axis with this one card added takes the deck from one class answered to four — creature, artifact, enchantment, land — because "Destroy target permanent" is the catch-all the strategy corpus says "earns its premium" [strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite]; without it a turn-3 Cursed Totem switches off Carrion Feeder, Viscera Seer, Yawgmoth and all four mana dorks and the deck simply loses.
ten.unlocks: The first answer to a non-creature permanent this deck has ever had, at instant speed, and the 3/3 Beast it hands back is a legal Hapatra target.

ten.why: Yawgmoth is the deck's one free repeatable -1/-1 source and every pass of his loop costs 1 life and draws a card; Ayara puts a drain and a lifegain on each black body that re-enters, which is what turns that loop from a draw engine into a kill — and Nest of Scarabs' Insect tokens are black, so she also drains on every batch of counters.
ten.unlocks: A life-neutral, table-wide drain attached to the loop the deck can actually run, plus a sacrifice outlet that draws.

ten.why: One green mana, instant speed, artifact or enchantment: this is the card you hold up on the turn you combo, and it is the cheapest out to Grafdigger's Cage, Cursed Totem, Torpor Orb and Rest in Peace — the corpus caps interaction at "essentially the most any player should pay" of three mana [strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite] and this comes in at one.
ten.unlocks: An answer castable under a stax tax, on the same turn as a two-mana commander.

ten.why: Graveyard is one of the four classes the audit reads as uncovered, and recomputing breadth with the Ooze added takes the deck to the fifth class and hits the target of five — "cover the classes — creature, artifact, enchantment, graveyard, land — before doubling any" [strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite]; it is targeted rather than symmetric, which matters because this deck's own Gravecrawler, Reassembling Skeleton and Phyrexian Reclamation all live in the yard.
ten.unlocks: Repeatable, one-mana-at-a-time yard exile that grows into a real body, without a Rest in Peace effect that would tax the deck's own recursion.

ten.why: Three mana whose entry alone puts two -1/-1 counters on a creature you control — one Hapatra trigger for a Snake, two Insects off Nest of Scarabs — and it is a Zombie, which is the permanent enabler Gravecrawler needs on the battlefield; the tagged Mikaeus lines are listed but they still name Mikaeus, so they thicken the kill rather than replace it.
ten.unlocks: A menace body that pays the counter engines on entry and drains each opponent on every Zombie death.

ten.why: The obsolescence index calls this a strictly-better Lotus Petal, and the read holds here: a two-mana commander plus Mikaeus, Yawgmoth, Yahenni and Sephiroth means it taps for colour on every turn after the second instead of once, and the Petal's one-shot is worth least in a deck already over its ramp target.
ten.unlocks: A repeatable colour source in a zero-mana slot, which is what a {B}{B}{B} Ayara and a {3}{B}{B}{B} Mikaeus actually want.

gaps: Blowfly Infestation is the thinnest engine component in the deck — one card, 16.3% assembled — and the audit's closer search returns nothing on either route: no pool card shares a role signature with a singleton, and no combo line pairs it with anything already sleeved. Whether a proliferate outlet substitutes for it is a question no artifact here has asked.

Plague Belcher's Mikaeus lines look bounded, not infinite: aimed at itself the Belcher nets one -1/-1 counter per pass against a base toughness of 4, and aimed anywhere else it returns carrying a +1/+1 counter that switches undying off. A stack scenario should pin the iteration count before anyone calls it a kill.

Gravecrawler + Phyrexian Altar is the channel's most popular line at 60,592 saves, but the record names no second Zombie and the recursion clause needs one on the battlefield while Gravecrawler is in the yard. Carrion Feeder, Host of the Hereafter and Mikaeus each satisfy it; the three-card Pitiless Plunderer lines name their enabler outright and are the safer citation.
Ayara + Yawgmoth + Mikaeus draws a card per iteration, so the kill is a race between 120 points of drain and the library. Nobody has run that arithmetic against this decklist.

card-advantage reads UNDER at 8 against a target of 10, but the audit names Grim Backwoods, The One Ring and Yawgmoth as showing the function uncounted — 11 on a fair read. Treated as a question, so no slot was spent on generic draw.
